content: 1. Praziquantel Indications and Dosage: Praziquantel is indicated for the treatment of schistosomiasis caused by all species of Schistosoma. The recommended dosage is 20 mg/kg orally, three times daily (TID) for one day, with doses spaced 4-6 hours apart. For clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis caused by liver flukes (Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini), the recommended dosage is 25 mg/kg orally, TID for one day, with 4-6 hour intervals between doses. For infections caused by Hymenolepis nana, a single dose of 5-10 mg/kg is recommended, or 25 mg/kg if necessary. 2. Pediatric Use: For children under 1 year of age, the safety and efficacy of praziquantel have not been established. For children aged 1 year and older, the dosage for schistosomiasis is 20 mg/kg orally, TID for one day, with 4-6 hour intervals. For liver fluke infections, the dosage is 25 mg/kg orally, TID for one day. 3. Drug Interactions: Apalutamide: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use is contraindicated. Carbamazepine: Decreases praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. Dexamethasone: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use is contraindicated. Enzalutamide: Decreases praziquantel levels through CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. Etravirine: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue etravirine two weeks before starting praziquantel and resume one day after the last praziquantel dose. Fosphenytoin: Decreases praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use is contraindicated. Mitotane: Decreases praziquantel levels through CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. Oxcarbazepine: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use is contraindicated. Phenobarbital: Decreases praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. Phenytoin: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use is contraindicated. Primidone: Decreases praziquantel levels through CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. Rifampin: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use is contraindicated. St. John’s Wort: Decreases praziquantel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Use is contraindicated. 4. Drugs to Avoid or Use with Caution: Amobarbital: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Armodafinil: Decreases praziquantel levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Belzutifan: Reduces praziquantel levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Drugs That Increase Praziquantel Levels: Fexinidazole: Increases praziquantel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib: Increases praziquantel levels through strong CYP3A inhibition. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates.
